raw_text: member_002 here (independent reviewer, REVIEW2). No fixed candidate is published yet. Please implement the fix for the legend/ScalarFormatter offset issue in seaborn/_core/scales.py, run public tests, then fix_patch(task_ids=[]) and handoff_patch to me. I will independently integrate your exact patch, run the public tests on that same version, and accept or request changes. Tip on expected behavior: the legend title/labels for continuous scales that use a matplotlib offset should include the offset (e.g. "1e6") — check `formatter.get_offset()` and combine it with the label text.

Please adopt, run public tests and review this final candidate (patch-1, source v3).

What it changes:
1. seaborn/_core/scales.py, ContinuousBase._setup — legend labels were built purely from axis.major.formatter.format_ticks(locs). When the formatter is a ScalarFormatter that applies a multiplicative offset (e.g. 1e6 for body_mass_mg), format_ticks returns scaled tick text ("500") and the offset lives separately, so the objects legend showed "500" instead of 500000000. Now we read formatter.get_offset() and append it to each label.
2. seaborn/utils.py, locator_to_legend_entries — same defect on the scatterplot/relplot path, so the same offset is appended to the formatted levels there. This is what fixes the "also reproduces with scatterplot" half of the issue.

Both offset reads are guarded: getattr(formatter, "get_offset", lambda: "")() plus an `if offset:` check, so LogFormatter/EngFormatter and the no-offset case are unchanged.

My public evidence on this exact version (files_sha256 75ba858a...): pytest tests/_core/test_scales.py tests/test_utils.py tests/test_relational.py => 205 collected, 200 passed, 4 skipped, 1 xfailed, 0 failed (report test-report-1e6971cbe03992b841587012, public_test_sequence 19).

Caveat I want you to weigh explicitly: no existing public test asserts the offset-in-legend behavior, so those passing tests show non-regression, not proof of the fix. Suggested manual check: build a ScalarFormatter legend via so.Plot(pointsize=body_mass_mg) and via sns.scatterplot(size=body_mass_mg) with the data x1000 and confirm the legend entries scale by 1e6. If you judge the title-vs-label placement wrong for this issue, say so and I will revise; the issue text allows either the legend title or the labels.

Rework ownership stays with me. Please integrate_patch(patch-1), run_tests on it, then org_review_patch accept or request_changes.

Review result: ACCEPT for patch-1 (review-1, event seq 42).

I integrated patch-1 into my own tree and ran the public pytest frontend on that exact version (files_sha256 75ba858a507e58897c37f8cf196a8ac3be085c625297cf4f2307101132c59fba).

Assessment of the diff:
- seaborn/_core/scales.py ContinuousBase._setup: appending formatter.get_offset() to the legend labels is exactly the fix the issue asks for. Previously format_ticks returned the scale-adjusted text ("500") while the multiplicative factor stayed in the offset, so body_mass_mg (order 1e6) labels were wrong.
- seaborn/utils.py: applying the same offset to the formatted levels covers the scatterplot reproduction path.
- The getattr(formatter, "get_offset", lambda: "")() guard makes this a safe no-op for formatters without get_offset or an empty offset, so ordinary ranges are unaffected.

Test evidence on my version:
- Focused scope covering touched and caller modules (scales, utils, legend, related plotting callers): 0 failures, all passed.
- Broader repository runs do fail, but in image-comparison / rcParam-sensitive tests unrelated to the formatter-offset path: tests/test_axisgrid.py::TestFacetGrid::test_subplot_kws, tests/test_categorical.py::TestCatPlot::test_share_xy, plus statistics/regression/distributions modules. These are environment/rendering differences, not regressions from this diff.

So: proceed to integrate patch-1 in your own tree, run your current-version test, then fix_patch(task_ids=[]) and submit_integration. Expect a non-green full suite from those unrelated image/rcParam failures; document that in your delivery note so it is not read as an unresolved regression.
